sentences.text: Japan needed a massive international airport, but there was no room on land, so they built an island in the ocean, which is slowly swallowing itself.
In the nineteen eighties, Osaka was running out of space, and residents hated noisy flights over the city.
Build a brand new artificial island five kilometers out in Osaka Bay, where nobody can complain.
Engineers flattened entire mountains, loaded millions of tons of rock onto barges, and dumped it into the sea.
The sea floor was made of about sixty feet of ultra-soft marine clay.
Instead of settling slightly, the island kept sinking, year after year, way faster than predicted.
To keep the terminal from flooding, engineers put hydraulic jacks under the building to lift it up by hand.
They surrounded the island with massive seawalls and armor blocks to stop typhoons from washing it away.
Pumping billions of dollars into keeping an airport above water is the ultimate engineering flex.
Despite sinking into the abyss, Kansai is still one of the most punctual airports on Earth.
With sea levels rising, engineers are now in a high-stakes race against Neptune himself.
Next time your flight is delayed, remember the runway under you is slowly drowning.
Send this to anyone who loves extreme civil engineering.
